thread:
Katie: Quick heads-up — we finished the lookahead-batcher v1 canary and the numbers look solid. p50 down ~12ms, p95 down ~38ms, p99 down ~85ms on chat workloads; cost per 1k tokens dropped ~9%.
Omar: Nice! Is that across both short and long sequences or just the short-path traffic?
Katie: Both. We ran separate benches — short (<=128) and mixed (avg 420). Short path saw the biggest p50 win, mixed had ~6% cost drop but big p99 improvements from reduced reorders.
Priya: Any perf regressions on CPU-bound tails or on seq>2k?
Katie: No regressions observed. We did targeted stress tests at 2k+ and memory overhead stayed within budget. Also validated KV cache hit behavior (no extra misses).
Matt: Can you paste the canary metrics and the rollout plan?
Katie: Canary summary (abridged):
```
canary: lookahead-batcher-v1
duration: 6h
routes: chat.real-time, chat.background
requests: 1.2M
p50: -12ms
p95: -38ms
p99: -85ms
cpu: +1.7% (avg), gpu_util: -2.4% (avg)
cost_per_1k_tokens: -9%
errors: no increase
```
Rollout plan: canary -> 25% (24h) -> 50% (48h) -> global. Auto-fallback to existing batcher on p99 breach or error spike.
lookahead-bot: canary deploy finished: all checks passed (latency, errors, cost) — 6h window.
Omar: Great. Any special config knobs? I saw `sequence_lookahead=8` in the canary.
Katie: Yeah we added two new knobs you might want to review: `sequence_lookahead` and `reorder_threshold`. Defaults used in canary: `sequence_lookahead=8`, `reorder_threshold=0.12`.
Priya: We should add metrics to console: queue_reorders, lookahead_applied_ratio, and per-route p99 delta. I'll open the ticket.
Matt: Who owns the rollback runbook if something weird happens?
Katie: SRE owns the rollback execution — I updated the runbook note in the canary doc. Quick steps: flip route to classic-batcher, scale lookahead pods down, purge prefix cache entries if needed.
Priya: I'll update docs + changelog and add a short writeup for customer-facing notes (impact 9% lower cost on average).
Omar: Can we gate enabling it for Dedicated customers? Some have strict latency SLAs.
Katie: Yes — rollout will be default-off for Dedicated and require opt-in via route policy. We coordinated with product.
Matt: LGTM. Can we schedule a quick 15m sync tomorrow to confirm console dashboards and smoke tests?
Katie: Sure — 11:15am. I'll invite the relevant folks. Thanks team :tada:
Omar: :thumbsup:
Priya: Nice work!
Katie: Merging canary results doc into /docs/internal/runtime/ and creating the public changelog blurb after rollout completes.
